newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Morkels swells despite interim profit dip.
newsitem.headline: Morkels swells despite interim profit dip.

text.p: Despite shrinking interim earnings slightly, Morkels Retail Group swelled its market value by almost 10 percent on Monday.
Dealers said that the acquistion of Bertrad in May had coloured profits and that removing Bertrad from results showed Morkels remaining operations performed more than satisfactorily.
By 1314 GMT Morkels had added 45 cents or 9.78 percent to 505 cents -- its intraday high and a new year high from 490 cents -- amid a volume of 11,800 shares.
"Look at the results and on the surface they might not seem too great but they were weighed by the acquistion of Bertrad. (Morkels) shows a very high rate of growth," a dealer said.
Morkels announced half-year earnings per share of 15.6 cents from 17.1 cents previously. No dividend was declared.
One dealer said that without Bertrad, Morkels businesses would have grown earnings by 60 percent.
